items.headline: It finally measured what the motif stage predicts before the recurrent layer touches it, and three things it told you flip. The auxiliary loss is the single biggest interpretability lever — the from-scratch run with it scores 0.4459 on site selection ahead of the recurrent layer, against 0.2590 for the weak sparsity penalty and roughly ten times the strong one — so its earlier "aux buys zero interpretability" is retracted; that claim came from counting motifs, which measures something else. Your argument for the lower sparsity penalty is now measured rather than eyeballed: the stronger penalty scores 0.0467, a 5.5-fold gap, and its better final correlation is just the recurrent layer covering for a motif stage that barely selects anything. And distillation does not make a model readable — the distilled run lands at 0.0787, below plain training. Sparse motifs and a meaningful motif stage are independent properties, not one.
items.why: The distillation phase as written assumes distilled models are the interpretable ones, and that assumption just failed measurement; the combination that might rescue it — distillation with the auxiliary loss and the small 8-unit recurrent layer — has never been run.
